status: Built (2026-10-05) by tools/materials/postprocess.py into assets/textures/<name>.png; see the material-maker skill. No engine code reads these layers yet. The ramps are first choices made by eye on the contact sheet (docs/screenshots/materials/contact-sheet.png), not decisions.
_rules: This file is the one source for Star Crew's surface materials: which Material Maker graph each comes from, its size in the world, and how its render is post-processed. The deck build, the mockups and the engine read it; nothing keeps a second list.
Every material is one layer of one texture array. Every layer is 128 x 128 px (layers.px), RGBA8, whatever the material.

Interior layers span 2.0 m, so 64 px per metre; exterior layers span 4.0 m, so 32 px per metre (layers.*_span_m). A surface's UVs are its world position divided by its material's span_m, so texel density never changes between materials of the same space.

tile_m is the world size of one repeat of the graph. A graph smaller than the span is tiled k x k inside the layer; a graph larger than the span gives the layer its top-left 1/k. Either way span_m / tile_m (or its inverse) is whole, so the layer tiles seamlessly.
Sampling: nearest on magnification, mipmapped on minification (layers.mag_filter, layers.min_filter), so a wall up close shows crisp texels and a far one does not shimmer.

The baked vertex light multiplies the texel. There is no per-pixel lighting on the Pi 5, so a graph's normal map and occlusion are baked into the albedo under one fixed key light from the top of the layer (bake.key_light_tangent), by relief.

Alpha is the emission mask: 255 shows the texel at full brightness whatever the light, 0 lights it only by the baked vertex light; in between blends the two. Non-emissive layers have alpha 0 everywhere, so an image viewer shows them as transparent; their colour is intact. Never premultiply alpha or let a tool strip colour under zero alpha.

Knobs, with postprocess.py DEFAULTS for any left out: ramp [[r, g, b] dark, [r, g, b] light] in 0-1 sRGB recolours by luminance, stretched so the material's darkest texels (bake.ramp_stretch_percentiles low) take the dark colour and its lightest the light one (default none); ramp_mix 0-1 blends the ramp over the original (default 1); relief 0-1 blends the albedo toward albedo * shade (default 1); relief_ambient 0-1 is the shade of a face turned away from the key light (default 0.45); colours 2-256 is a median-cut palette per layer, null for none (default 32); emissive true takes the alpha from the graph's emission map (default false).
layer is the material's index in the array. It is stable: a compiled deck names materials by it. Add a material at the end; never renumber.
Units: metres (_m), pixels (px), sRGB colour components in 0-1.

layers.format: RGBA8: sRGB colour, linear alpha (the emission mask)
